items.name: adjudication
items.description: Answers pharmacy claims: the claim switch path, its system of record, its cache and its queues. The business success bar.
items.businessImpact: A claim that cannot be adjudicated is a prescription that is not dispensed. Pharmacies fall back to a manual paper process within minutes and the partner clearinghouse begins queueing; the BIA puts the tolerance at one hour.
items.notes: The BIA's 15-minute RPO is TIGHTER than the workspace-level RPO of 30 min that engineering proposed and that nobody has approved (workspace.objectives). Nothing has reconciled the two, and the 118 min measured on the remittance path in test #2 misses both. Reconciling them is a governance item, not a data question.

items.name: remittance
items.description: Imports and settles remittance advice (ERA), including the bank SFTP path and the settlement object store.
items.businessImpact: Settlement files that miss the banking window delay payment to pharmacies by a full cycle. The BIA accepts one business hour of lost remittance records; it does not accept silent loss, so a recovery point that cannot be dated is treated as a miss.
items.notes: Tier 0 with a looser objective than adjudication, because settlement is a batch cycle rather than an interactive path. The measured 118-min RPA in test #2 is a miss against this 60-min RPO too — this service owns the only Tier-0 store still on point-in-time recovery (gap_rpa1).

items.name: pharmacy
items.description: Pharmacy master data. Not in the success bar itself, but adjudication cannot answer a claim without it.
items.notes: Tier 1 in the BIA, but it is a hard dependency of a Tier-0 service. Read the pair honestly: the adjudication 60-min RTO cannot be met while its dependency is allowed four hours. This is the most common way a tiering exercise contradicts itself, and it is written down here rather than smoothed over.

items.name: pricing
items.description: Drug pricing lookups used during adjudication, its reference store and its cache.
items.notes: The 24-hour RPO is deliberate and matches the mechanism: pricing reference data is reloaded from the drug-price feed weekly, so a daily AWS Backup copy loses nothing that the next feed does not replace (see cmp_aurora_pricing). A store whose RPO is a day is a decision, not an oversight.

items.name: platform
items.description: The shared layer every service rides on: EKS, the VPC and its endpoints, IAM/OIDC, KMS, ACM, Secrets Manager, the API Gateway edge, the CDN/WAF allowlist and the public DNS flip.
items.notes: No business objective of its own, on purpose. The BIA sets objectives for business services, and the platform inherits the tightest one riding on it — today that is adjudication at 60/15. Copying 60/15 onto this row would invent an approval that no BIA ever gave, so the numbers are left null and the inheritance is stated instead. Tier 0 because everything Tier 0 depends on it.

items.name: adjudication
items.description: Staging adjudication: the claim path the partner integration tests against on the staging domain.
items.notes: No BIA objective: staging is not recovered in an event. Its value to the DR program is the partner test claim, which is the only place the clearinghouse path is exercised at all.

items.name: adjudication
items.description: Dev adjudication: the service the August and September recovery tests recover and then push a test claim through.
items.notes: No business objective — dev is the rehearsal estate. It is still the service that produced the workspace's only real RTA number, because it is where the success bar was attempted.

items.description: Dev remittance: ERA import, its point-in-time store and the settlement bucket the drill writes into.
items.notes: No business objective. This is the service the 118-min RPA was measured on: the dev remittance store is protected by the same third-party point-in-time recovery, on the same schedule, as the production one.
